  • A simple DC motor can be built with a battery, a magnet, paper-clip supports and a coil whose ends are half-insulated so the current flows for only half of each cycle, like a commutator.
  • In the supply system a generation transformer steps about 13 kV up to 500 kV for transmission, and distribution transformers step 11 kV down to 220 V for homes.

Solved Exercises

Projects

Q: GROUP A 'ELECTROMAGNET': Build an electromagnet as an activity in this chapter. See how much the strength of electromagnet change by changing the current flow by using different batteries or increasing the number of turns in the coil or having other core materials (such as pencil, steel nail etc.) instead of iron nail. Summerize your findings in an article for school magazine.

Ans: Build and test it as in the Activity 'Build an Electromagnet'. (1) Construction: wrap copper wire in a coil around an iron nail and connect the ends of the wire to the two terminals of a cell; the system forms an electromagnet and attracts objects such as paper pins just like a magnet (caution from the book: it becomes hot in use - drop it if it becomes uncomfortably hot). (2) Test of current: use one cell, then two cells in series - the larger current picks up more pins, so the strength increases with current. (3) Test of turns: increase the number of turns of the coil - more turns pick up more pins, so the strength increases with the number of turns. (4) Test of core: replace the iron nail with a pencil (wood) or a steel nail - with the non-magnetic pencil core the coil alone is weak, while iron gives a strong field because the field lines are concentrated in the core, as with the solenoid of Section 15.1.2. Summarise these three findings - strength grows with current, with turns, and with a soft-iron core - in the magazine article.

Q: GROUP B 'MAGNETIC EFFECT OF CURRENT': Research the application of the magnetic effect of an electric current in relay, door latch, loudspeaker, and circuit breaker from the internet and school library, and present your findings in classroom.

Ans: Present the findings under the four devices, each based on a current producing a magnetic field (Section 15.1). (1) Relay: a small current in a coil makes it an electromagnet which attracts an iron armature and closes (or opens) contacts in a second, larger circuit - a small current safely controls a large one. (2) Door latch / electric bell type devices: the electromagnet attracts an iron latch or striker when current flows and releases it when the current stops. (3) Loudspeaker (moving-coil, from this unit): the radial magnetic field of a permanent magnet exerts a force on the voice coil proportional to the current in it; the amplifier signal makes the current oscillate in direction and magnitude, the coil and the attached cone oscillate with it, and sound is produced - turning up the volume increases the current amplitude and the loudness. (4) Circuit breaker: an excessive current strengthens the electromagnet (or heating element) inside the breaker so that it pulls the contact apart and breaks the circuit, protecting the wiring, and it can then be reset. Present each with the common principle: no current, no magnetic effect.

Q: GROUP C 'MAGNETISM AND TECHNOLOGY': Identify different technologies related to magnetism such as electric motors and generators, medical equipment, loudspeakers, magnetic information storage devices. Write its historical over view relating when, how and where these devices were first formed. Write an essay for school magazine.

Ans: Write the essay device by device, tying each to this unit. (1) Electric motor: based on the force and torque on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field (Sections 15.2-15.4); developed in the 19th century after Oersted showed that a current produces a magnetic field and Faraday showed the force on a conductor - the DC motor uses a split-ring commutator so the coil keeps rotating in one direction. (2) Generator: based on Faraday's electromagnetic induction (Section 15.5) - a changing magnetic field induces an emf; the AC generator rotates a coil between magnet poles and takes the current out through slip rings. (3) Loudspeaker: the moving-coil speaker applies the force on a current-carrying wire in the field of a permanent magnet to a paper cone. (4) Medical equipment and magnetic information storage: strong electromagnets and magnetic fields are used in hospital scanners, and data is stored as magnetised patterns on discs and tapes, both descendants of the electromagnet and solenoid of Section 15.1. For each device state when and where it was first made, how it works, and the principle from this chapter that it uses.

Q: GROUP D 'ELECTRIC MOTOR AND GENERATOR': Read literature and search how different motors and generators can be easily made. Build a simple DC Motor or AC Generator for your school laboratory.

Ans: Build one device following the book's activities. For a simple DC motor (Activity 'Build a simple DC motor'): (1) attach a magnet on the side of a battery with adhesive tape; (2) shape one end of each of two paper clips into a small loop at the top and fix the clips on the ends of the battery with tape as supports and contacts; (3) make 10 to 15 coils of wire, scrape the insulation at the ends, and colour one side at each end with a permanent marker to insulate that side - this prevents current flowing for half of every cycle and has the same effect as a commutator; (4) mount the coil in the two paper-clip loops and let the motor spin: the coil, in the magnet's field, experiences the torque of Section 15.3 and rotates. Alternatively build the AC generator form: rotate a coil between the poles of a permanent magnet and take the induced alternating emf out through slip rings and brushes (Figure 15.10). Label the parts - coil, magnet, brushes, split ring or slip rings - and place the model in the school laboratory.

Q: GROUP E 'TRANSFORMERS': Make a list of the use of transformers (step-up and step-down) for various purposes in your home. Make a chart and display it in your classroom.

Ans: Make the chart on the model of Figure 15.16 (Transmission of Power). Home and supply uses to list: (1) Step-up at the power plant: the generation transformer raises about 13 kV to 500 kV for the high-voltage transmission lines, reducing current and therefore power loss P = I^2 R in the lines. (2) Step-down at substations: transmission voltage is reduced in stages (132 kV, 66 kV, 11 kV) for heavy industry, light industry and distribution. (3) Step-down at the pole near the home: distribution transformers reduce 11 kV to 220 V for homes. (4) Inside the home: small step-down transformers/adapters in chargers and appliances reduce 220 V AC to the low voltages the devices need (for example a 12 V lamp transformer), while a step-up transformer is used where a higher voltage is needed, as in the X-ray unit of Example 15.3. For each entry show input voltage, output voltage, and whether Ns is greater or less than Np. Display the chart in the classroom.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Cathode rays are a beam of electrons emitted from the cathode of an evacuated tube.
  • An electric field applied parallel to an electron beam changes the speed of the electrons, while a magnetic field applied parallel to the beam does not change the state of the electrons.
  • An AND gate gives a high (1) output only when all its inputs are high (1), and an OR gate gives a high (1) output when one or more of its inputs are high (1).
  • A NAND gate gives a low (0) output only when all its inputs are high (1), and a NOR gate gives a low (0) output when one or more of its inputs are high (1).
  • The Boolean equation for the OR gate is X = A + B.
  • The Boolean equation for the NAND gate is X = AB with a bar over AB, that is X = NOT (AB).

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: 1. Cathode rays are beam of

Options: (a) protons (b) electrons (c) ions (d) neutrons

Correct answer: electrons

Q: 2. If electric field is applied parallel to the direction of electron beam, the electrons will

Options: (a) speed up (b) slow down (c) deflect (d) not change its state

Correct answer: slow down

Q: 3. If magnetic field is applied parallel to the direction of electron beam, the electrons will

Options: (a) speed up (b) slow down (c) deflect (d) not change its state

Correct answer: not change its state

Q: 4. The electronic circuit that gives high (1) output when all its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.

Options: (a) AND (b) OR (c) NAND (d) NOR

Correct answer: AND

Q: 5. The electronic circuit that gives high (1) output when one or more of its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.

Options: (a) AND (b) OR (c) NAND (d) NOR

Correct answer: OR

Q: 6. The electronic circuit that gives low (0) output when all its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.

Options: (a) AND (b) OR (c) NAND (d) NOR

Correct answer: NAND

Q: 7. The electronic circuit that gives low (0) output when one or more of its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.

Options: (a) AND (b) OR (c) NAND (d) NOR

Correct answer: NOR

Q: 8. The Boolean equation for OR gate is

Options: (a) X = AB (b) X = A + B (c) X = AB with bar over AB (d) X = A + B with bar over (A + B)

Correct answer: X = A + B

Q: 9. The Boolean equation for NAND gate is

Options: (a) X = AB (b) X = A + B (c) X = AB with bar over AB (d) X = A + B with bar over (A + B)

Correct answer: X = AB with bar over AB

mcqs.q: Cathode rays are beam of
mcqs.why: Cathode rays are a beam of fast-moving electrons emitted from the cathode of an evacuated tube, produced by thermionic emission in the electron gun.

mcqs.q: If electric field is applied parallel to the direction of electron beam, the electrons will
mcqs.why: A field parallel to the beam acts along the line of motion, so it changes the speed instead of deflecting the beam sideways. The electrons are negatively charged, so the force on them is opposite to the field direction along the beam, and they slow down.

mcqs.q: If magnetic field is applied parallel to the direction of electron beam, the electrons will
mcqs.why: A magnetic field exerts a force on moving electrons in any direction of motion other than the direction of the field itself. If the beam moves parallel to the field, no force acts, so the electrons do not change their state.

mcqs.q: The electronic circuit that gives high (1) output when all its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.
mcqs.why: The AND gate gives output 1 only when all its inputs are 1: A = 1, B = 1 gives X = 1, and every other input combination gives X = 0. Its Boolean equation is X = AB.

mcqs.q: The electronic circuit that gives high (1) output when one or more of its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.
mcqs.why: The OR gate gives output 1 when one or more of its inputs are 1; only A = 0, B = 0 gives X = 0. Its Boolean equation is X = A + B.

mcqs.q: The electronic circuit that gives low (0) output when all its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.
mcqs.why: The NAND gate is an AND gate with the output inverted, X = NOT (AB). It gives output 0 only when all its inputs are 1, and output 1 for every other combination of inputs.

mcqs.q: The electronic circuit that gives low (0) output when one or more of its input are high (1) is called _____ gate.
mcqs.why: The NOR gate is an OR gate with the output inverted, X = NOT (A + B). As soon as one or more inputs are 1 the output is 0; it gives output 1 only when all its inputs are 0.

mcqs.q: The Boolean equation for OR gate is
options: X = AB with bar over AB
X = A + B with bar over (A + B)
mcqs.why: The OR operation is written as addition in Boolean algebra, so the OR gate output is X = A + B, which is 1 whenever A or B (or both) is 1.

mcqs.q: The Boolean equation for NAND gate is
options: X = AB with bar over AB
X = A + B with bar over (A + B)
mcqs.why: NAND means NOT AND: first the inputs are ANDed to give AB, and then the result is inverted, so the Boolean equation is X = AB with a bar over AB, that is X = NOT (AB).

mcqs.q: How many input combinations are possible for a logic gate with 4 inputs?
mcqs.why: Formula: number of combinations = 2^n, where n is the number of inputs. Substitution: 2^4 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16. Result: 16 combinations.

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Free electrons are the valence electrons in the outermost shells of metal atoms, not bound to any particular atom and free to move randomly through the whole metal.
  • The work function is the definite amount of energy needed to pull a free electron out of the metal surface.
  • The accelerating anode, kept at a high positive potential, attracts electrons from the hot cathode and accelerates them so they pass through its central hole as a fast, fine beam.
  • A full television picture appears because the deflection system sweeps the beam very rapidly across the whole screen line by line, and our eyes join the glowing spots together.
  • A magnet brought near a CRT distorts the image because its field deflects the electron beam, so electrons strike the screen at wrong positions.
  • Cathode ray particles are negatively charged: between charged parallel plates the beam bends towards the positive plate.
  • A logic gate with 4 inputs has 2^4 = 16 possible input combinations.
  • An AND gate gives a high output only when all its inputs are high, while a NOR gate gives a high output only when all its inputs are low.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Conceptual Questions (Give a brief response to the following questions)

Q: 1. What are free electrons?

Ans: In a metal, the electrons in the outermost shells of the atoms are not bound to any particular atom. These valence electrons are free to move randomly through the whole metal and are called free electrons. They are, however, still bound to the material as a whole, and a definite amount of energy, called the work function, is needed to pull them out of the metal surface.

Q: 2. What is the function of an accelerating anode in an electron gun?

Ans: The accelerating anode is kept at a high positive potential with respect to the cathode. It attracts the electrons emitted from the hot cathode and accelerates them to high speed, so that they pass through its central hole as a fast, fine beam of electrons.

Q: 3. If the electron beam in a television tube is striking just one point on the screen at a time, how can we get a full picture? Explain.

Ans: The deflection system of the tube sweeps the electron beam very rapidly across the whole screen, line by line, in a sawtooth scanning pattern. At each instant the beam makes one glowing spot (pixel) of a certain brightness on the phosphor screen. The scanning is so fast, and each spot glows briefly, that our eyes join all the spots together and we see one complete, steady picture.

Q: 4. Why image is distorted when a magnet is brought close to old television screens or monitors with cathode ray tube (CRT) inside?

Ans: Cathode rays (the electron beam) are deflected by a magnetic field. When a magnet is brought near the CRT, its field bends the paths of the electrons inside the tube, so the electrons strike the screen at wrong positions instead of their correct pixels. The spots of the picture are displaced, and the image appears distorted.

Q: 5. Assuming that cathode rays are a beam of charged particles, how could you demonstrate that these particles are negatively charged? Explain.

Ans: Pass the cathode ray beam between two oppositely charged parallel plates, i.e. through an electric field. The beam is observed to bend towards the positive plate and away from the negative plate. Since opposite charges attract, the particles of the beam must carry a negative charge. The direction of deflection of the beam in a magnetic field confirms the same result.

Q: 6. If there are 4 inputs in any logic gate, how many combinations are possible?

Ans: Given: number of inputs, n = 4
Formula: Number of combinations = 2^n
Substitution: 2^4
= 2 x 2 x 2 x 2
= 16
Answer: 16 combinations

Q: 7. What conditions produce a high (1) output for an AND gate and NOR gate?

Ans: An AND gate gives a high (1) output only when ALL its inputs are high (1).
AND gate: A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 0; A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0; A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0; A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 1
A NOR gate gives a high (1) output only when ALL its inputs are low (0).
NOR gate: A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 1; A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0; A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0; A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 0

Q: 8. What are the algebraic Boolean expressions to represent the output of AND, OR, NOT, NAND and NOR gates?

Ans: AND gate: X = A.B, written as X = AB
OR gate: X = A + B
NOT gate: X = A with bar over A (NOT A)
NAND gate: X = AB with bar over AB, i.e. X = NOT (AB)
NOR gate: X = A + B with bar over (A + B), i.e. X = NOT (A + B)

mcqs.q: Free electrons in a metal are
options: electrons tightly bound to one atom
valence electrons not bound to any particular atom, free to move through the whole metal
mcqs.why: In a metal, the electrons in the outermost shells of the atoms are not bound to any particular atom. These valence electrons are free to move randomly through the whole metal and are called free electrons.

mcqs.q: The work function of a metal is
options: the energy needed to pull a free electron out of the metal surface
the voltage of the accelerating anode
the energy of the electron beam in the tube
mcqs.why: Free electrons are still bound to the material as a whole, and a definite amount of energy, called the work function, is needed to pull them out of the metal surface; thermionic emission occurs when an electron gains more than this energy.

mcqs.q: The function of the accelerating anode in an electron gun is to
options: attract the emitted electrons and accelerate them to high speed
deflect the beam across the screen
control the brightness of the spot
mcqs.why: The accelerating anode is kept at a high positive potential with respect to the cathode. It attracts the electrons emitted from the hot cathode and accelerates them to high speed, so they pass through its central hole as a fast, fine beam.

mcqs.q: Although the electron beam in a television tube strikes just one point of the screen at a time, we see a full picture because
options: the screen stores the whole picture at once
many beams strike the screen together
the beam stays on one line only
the beam is swept very rapidly across the whole screen line by line and our eyes join the spots together
mcqs.why: The deflection system sweeps the beam very rapidly across the whole screen in a sawtooth scanning pattern, each instant making one glowing spot. The scanning is so fast, and each spot glows briefly, that our eyes join all the spots into one complete, steady picture.

mcqs.q: The image on an old CRT television is distorted when a magnet is brought close to the screen because the magnet's field
options: deflects the electron beam so electrons strike the screen at wrong positions
stops the electron gun emitting electrons
changes the colour of the phosphor
mcqs.why: Cathode rays are deflected by a magnetic field. The field of the nearby magnet bends the paths of the electrons inside the tube, so they strike the screen at wrong positions instead of their correct pixels and the picture appears distorted.

mcqs.q: To show that cathode ray particles are negatively charged, the beam is passed between oppositely charged parallel plates and it is observed to
mcqs.why: Between the charged plates the beam bends towards the positive plate and away from the negative plate. Since opposite charges attract, the particles of the beam must carry a negative charge.

mcqs.q: If there are 4 inputs in any logic gate, the number of possible input combinations is
mcqs.why: Formula: number of combinations = 2^n, where n is the number of inputs. Substitution: 2^4 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. Step: 2 x 2 = 4, 4 x 2 = 8, 8 x 2 = 16. Result: 16 combinations.

mcqs.q: An AND gate produces a high (1) output
options: when at least one input is high
only when all its inputs are high
when all its inputs are low
when exactly one input is high
mcqs.why: From the AND truth table, A = 0, B = 0 gives X = 0; A = 0, B = 1 gives X = 0; A = 1, B = 0 gives X = 0; only A = 1, B = 1 gives X = 1, so the output is high only when all inputs are high.

mcqs.q: A NOR gate produces a high (1) output
options: only when all its inputs are low
when at least one input is high
when all its inputs are high
mcqs.why: From the NOR truth table, only A = 0, B = 0 gives X = 1; A = 0, B = 1, A = 1, B = 0 and A = 1, B = 1 all give X = 0, so the NOR output is high only when all inputs are low.

mcqs.q: The Boolean expression for the output of a NOT gate with input A is
options: X = A with bar over A, that is NOT A
mcqs.why: The NOT gate inverts its single input, so its Boolean expression is X = A with a bar over A, written as X = NOT A: input 0 gives output 1 and input 1 gives output 0.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Electrons are emitted from a heated filament by thermionic emission: when a free electron gains heat energy greater than the work function, it escapes from the metal surface.
  • Cathode rays are a beam of fast-moving electrons, produced in an electron gun where the heated cathode emits electrons and the anodes speed them up and squeeze them into a narrow beam.
  • In the electron gun the negative control grid controls the number of electrons passing through, and so controls the brightness of the beam, while the focusing anode narrows the stream into a fine pencil-like beam.
  • An electric field deflects an electron beam towards the positive plate, and a magnetic field also deflects the beam, except when the beam moves parallel to the field, when no force acts.
  • The CRO uses an electron gun, vertical and horizontal deflection plates and a fluorescent screen coated with zinc sulphide (ZnS); its uses include displaying waveforms, measuring short time intervals and measuring potential difference.
  • In analogue electronics quantities vary continuously, while in digital electronics they take only two discrete values, ON (1) and OFF (0), such as +5 V for ON and 0 V for OFF.
  • A logic gate is an electronic circuit that takes one or more binary inputs and produces a single binary output according to a definite logical rule.
  • In automatic light switching an AND gate with an LDR and a timer switches the bulb ON only when both inputs are high, and in a textile coloring plant a NOR gate raises an alarm only when both colour tanks are low.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Comprehensive Questions (Give an extended response to the following questions)

Q: 1. Why electrons are emitted from an electrically heated metal filament?

Ans: The free electrons inside a metal are held within the metal by its work function. When an electric current is passed through a metal filament (such as tungsten), the filament becomes hot. The heat energy is transferred to the free electrons, and when an electron gains energy greater than the work function it escapes from the metal surface. This emission of electrons by heating is called thermionic emission. The higher the temperature of the filament, the greater is the number of electrons emitted.

Q: 2. What are cathode rays? How are cathode rays produced?

Ans: Cathode rays are a beam of fast-moving electrons emitted from the cathode of an evacuated tube. They are produced in an electron gun: a cathode is heated indirectly by a filament, and by thermionic emission it releases electrons. The control grid regulates the number of electrons passing through, and the positively charged accelerating and focusing anodes speed the electrons up and squeeze them into a narrow beam, which leaves the gun as cathode rays inside the vacuum tube.

Q: 3. Describe the construction and working of electron gun?

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure shows a cylindrical assembly inside the neck of the vacuum tube. At the left is the Cylinder containing the Hot cathode, which is heated indirectly by a filament (about 600 mA current at 6.3 V) and is coated with barium and strontium oxide to emit electrons easily. Next to it is the Control Grid, a nickel cylinder with a small hole, kept at a negative potential to control the number of electrons. After the grid is the Accelerating anode (+), a cylinder at high positive potential, and then the Focusing anode (+), which narrows the stream. The Electron beam leaves the gun from the right side.
Working: the heated cathode emits electrons by thermionic emission. The negative control grid pushes back some electrons, so changing its voltage controls the brightness (intensity) of the beam. The accelerating anode pulls the electrons forward at high speed, and the focusing anode focuses them into a fine pencil-like beam that travels down the tube.

Q: 4. What effect does an electric field and magnetic field have on the electron beam?

Ans: Effect of electric field: an electron beam is deflected by an electric field. The electrons are attracted towards the positive plate and repelled by the negative plate, so between the deflection plates the beam bends towards the positive plate; the stronger the field, the greater the deflection.
Effect of magnetic field: a magnetic field also exerts a force on the moving electrons and deflects the beam. The force acts in any direction of motion of the charged particles other than the direction of the magnetic field itself; if the beam moves parallel to the field, no force acts. The direction of the force is found by the right-hand rule / Fleming's left-hand rule. Both effects are used to steer the beam in the cathode ray tube.

Q: 5. Describe the working principle of Cathode Ray Oscilloscope (CRO) and make list of its uses.

Ans: The CRO is built around a cathode ray tube. Its main parts are: (1) the electron gun, which produces a fine beam of electrons; (2) the deflection system, consisting of a pair of vertical deflection plates and a pair of horizontal deflection plates, which move the beam up-down and left-right by applying voltages; and (3) the fluorescent screen, coated with a phosphor such as zinc sulphide (ZnS), which glows where the beam strikes it. The signal to be examined is applied to the vertical plates while a sawtooth voltage sweeps the beam horizontally, so the waveform of the signal is drawn on the screen.
Uses of CRO: displaying waveforms of electrical signals; measuring short time intervals; measuring potential difference (it can be used as a voltmeter); troubleshooting malfunctioned electronic equipment; and checking newly designed circuitry.

Q: 6. What is the difference between analogue and digital electronics?

Ans: In analogue electronics the quantities vary continuously and can take infinitely many values between a minimum and a maximum; analogue signals are smooth, continuously varying voltages or currents. In digital electronics the quantities take only two discrete values, ON and OFF, represented by 1 and 0; for example +5 V is ON (1) and 0 V is OFF (0). Analogue signals are changed into digital form by an ADC (analogue to digital converter), and digital signals are changed back by a DAC, so that modern devices can process information digitally.

Q: 7. Define logic gates. Describe the operation of AND, OR, NOT, NAND and NOR logic gates by drawing their symbols and truth tables.

Ans: A logic gate is an electronic circuit that takes one or more binary inputs (0 or 1) and produces a single binary output according to a definite logical rule.
AND gate: symbol is D-shaped (flat input side, rounded output side); Boolean equation X = AB. It gives output 1 only when all inputs are 1.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 1
OR gate: symbol has a curved input side and a pointed output side; Boolean equation X = A + B. It gives output 1 when one or more inputs are 1.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 1
NOT gate: symbol is a triangle with a small circle (bubble) at the output; Boolean equation X = NOT A. It inverts the single input.
A = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1 -> X = 0
NAND gate: symbol is an AND gate with a small circle (bubble) at the output; Boolean equation X = NOT (AB). It gives output 0 only when all inputs are 1.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 0
NOR gate: symbol is an OR gate with a small circle (bubble) at the output; Boolean equation X = NOT (A + B). It gives output 1 only when all inputs are 0.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 0

Q: 8. Explain simple uses of logic gates in (a) automatic light bulb switching (b) textile coloring plant.

Ans: (a) Automatic light bulb switching: an AND gate is used with two inputs, a light dependent resistor (LDR) and a timer. During the day the LDR gives a low (0) output. In the evening the LDR starts conducting and its output becomes high (1). The bulb glows only when the timer output is also high (1), i.e. when both inputs of the AND gate are 1, so the light switches ON automatically at the set time in the dark. An OR gate version can also be used, in which the light glows when either of the two conditions is met.
(b) Textile coloring plant: a NOR gate is used with level sensors fitted in two colour tanks. Each sensor gives a high (5 V) output when its tank is more than one-quarter (25%) full, and a low (0 V) output when the level falls to 25% or below. The NOR gate output becomes high (5 V) and raises an alarm only when BOTH tanks are low, warning the operator to refill the colour. A NAND gate with a green light can likewise show that both tanks are full.

mcqs.q: Electrons are emitted from an electrically heated metal filament because
options: the filament attracts electrons from the air
free electrons that gain heat energy greater than the work function escape from the metal surface
the electric current pushes electrons out mechanically
mcqs.why: When current heats the filament, the heat energy is transferred to the free electrons, and when an electron gains energy greater than the work function it escapes from the metal surface. This emission of electrons by heating is called thermionic emission.

mcqs.q: Cathode rays are produced in an electron gun when
options: a cold cathode absorbs electrons from the anode
a magnet sweeps electrons across a screen
the heated cathode emits electrons by thermionic emission and the anodes speed them into a narrow beam
gas inside the tube is ionised by a battery
mcqs.why: In the electron gun a cathode is heated indirectly by a filament and releases electrons by thermionic emission. The control grid regulates the number passing through, and the positively charged accelerating and focusing anodes speed the electrons up and squeeze them into a narrow beam.

mcqs.q: In the electron gun, changing the voltage of the negative control grid changes the brightness of the beam because the grid
options: controls the number of electrons passing through it
heats the cathode to a higher temperature
focuses the electrons into a fine beam
deflects the beam up and down
mcqs.why: The control grid is a nickel cylinder with a small hole, kept at a negative potential. It pushes back some electrons, so changing its voltage controls the number of electrons passing through, which controls the brightness (intensity) of the beam.

mcqs.q: When an electron beam passes between electric deflection plates, the beam bends
mcqs.why: Electrons are negatively charged, so in an electric field they are attracted towards the positive plate and repelled by the negative plate. Between the deflection plates the beam bends towards the positive plate, and the stronger the field, the greater the deflection.

mcqs.q: A magnetic field exerts no force on an electron beam when the beam moves
mcqs.why: The magnetic force acts in any direction of motion of the charged particles other than the direction of the magnetic field itself. If the beam moves parallel to the field, no force acts and the beam is not deflected.

mcqs.q: The fluorescent screen of a cathode ray tube is coated with a phosphor such as
mcqs.why: The CRO screen is coated with a phosphor such as zinc sulphide (ZnS), which glows where the electron beam strikes it, so the waveform drawn by the deflected beam becomes visible on the screen.

mcqs.q: In digital electronics, the quantities take
options: only two discrete values, ON (1) and OFF (0)
infinitely many values between a minimum and a maximum
mcqs.why: In digital electronics the quantities take only two discrete values, ON and OFF, represented by 1 and 0; for example +5 V is ON (1) and 0 V is OFF (0). This is unlike analogue electronics, where quantities vary continuously.

mcqs.q: A logic gate is best defined as an electronic circuit that
options: stores electric charge for later use
takes one or more binary inputs and produces a single binary output according to a definite logical rule
mcqs.why: A logic gate is an electronic circuit that takes one or more binary inputs (0 or 1) and produces a single binary output according to a definite logical rule, as shown by the truth tables of the AND, OR, NOT, NAND and NOR gates.

mcqs.q: In automatic light bulb switching, an AND gate is used with an LDR and a timer so that the bulb glows only when
options: both inputs of the AND gate are high (1)
mcqs.why: In the evening the LDR output becomes high (1) in the dark. The bulb glows only when the timer output is also high (1), that is when both inputs of the AND gate are 1, so the light switches ON automatically at the set time in the dark.

mcqs.q: In a textile coloring plant, the NOR gate alarm becomes high only when
options: one tank is full and one is low
both colour tanks are low, at 25% level or below
mcqs.why: Each level sensor gives a high output when its tank is more than one-quarter (25%) full and a low output at 25% or below. The NOR gate output becomes high, raising the alarm, only when both inputs are low, that is when both tanks are low and need refilling.

lessons.title: Projects
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The automatic water pump runs only when the roof tank is not full and the well has sufficient water: Output = (NOT A) AND B, using a NOT gate on the roof-tank sensor followed by an AND gate.
  • The front gate lamp uses an AND gate with an LDR darkness sensor and a pressure switch under the doormat, so the lamp is ON only when it is dark and someone stands on the doormat.
  • The classroom chart shows the symbols and truth tables of the NOT, OR, AND, NOR and NAND gates; the NOR and NAND symbols are the OR and AND symbols with a small circle (bubble) at the output.
  • CRT televisions were replaced by LED and LCD screens because a CRT set is bulky, deep and heavy and consumes more power, while LED and LCD screens are flat, thin, light and use much less power.
  • Modern life runs on digital electronics, in which signals are ON (1) or OFF (0), and computers are at the forefront of electronic technology.

Solved Exercises

Projects

Q: GROUP A 'AUTOMATIC WATER PUMP': Design logic circuit for automatic water pump. Pump will operate if there is an insufficient amount of water in the tank on the roof of house and sufficient amount of water in the well inside the house. Prepare a chart and present your finding to the class.

Ans: Take two inputs: A = sensor in the roof tank (A = 1 when the roof tank is full, A = 0 when it has insufficient water) and B = sensor in the well (B = 1 when the well has sufficient water, B = 0 when it does not). The pump must run only when the roof tank is NOT full (NOT A = 1) AND the well has sufficient water (B = 1), so the design uses a NOT gate on input A followed by an AND gate: Output = (NOT A) AND B.
Truth table of the circuit:
A = 0, B = 0 -> Pump = 0 (well is empty, pump stays OFF)
A = 0, B = 1 -> Pump = 1 (roof tank needs water and well has water, pump ON)
A = 1, B = 0 -> Pump = 0 (roof tank already full, pump OFF)
A = 1, B = 1 -> Pump = 0 (roof tank already full, pump OFF)
Prepare a chart showing the two sensors, the NOT gate, the AND gate, the truth table above and the pump, and present it to the class.

Q: GROUP B 'AUTOMATIC FRONT GATE LIGHTING SYSTEM': What types of logic gates can you use to build an automatic lighting mechanism at front gate of your house. Identify the sensors required and the logic gates when a lamp outside your home front gate comes on automatically when it is dark and someone stands on the doormat outside the front door. Prepare a chart and give a brief presentation to your class fellows.

Ans: An AND gate is used, because the lamp must glow only when BOTH conditions are true at the same time. Two sensors are required: (1) a light dependent resistor (LDR) which senses darkness and gives output 1 when it is dark and 0 in daylight, and (2) a pressure switch fitted under the doormat which gives output 1 when someone stands on the doormat and 0 when nobody is standing there.
Truth table of the system:
Dark = 0, Person on doormat = 0 -> Lamp = 0
Dark = 0, Person on doormat = 1 -> Lamp = 0 (daytime, lamp not needed)
Dark = 1, Person on doormat = 0 -> Lamp = 0 (dark but nobody at the gate)
Dark = 1, Person on doormat = 1 -> Lamp = 1 (dark and someone at the gate, lamp ON)
Prepare a chart of the sensors, the AND gate and this truth table, and present it to the class.

Q: GROUP C 'CHART MAKING': Prepare a chart of symbols and corresponding truth table for NOT, OR, AND, NOR and NAND gates to be displayed in your classroom.

Ans: NOT gate: symbol is a triangle with a small circle (bubble) at its output end; it has one input A and output X = NOT A.
A = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1 -> X = 0
OR gate: symbol is a curved-back gate with a pointed output end; output X = A + B.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 1
AND gate: symbol is a D-shaped (flat input side, rounded output side) gate; output X = A.B = AB.
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 1
NOR gate: symbol is an OR gate with a small circle (bubble) at the output; output X = NOT (A + B).
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 0
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 0
NAND gate: symbol is an AND gate with a small circle (bubble) at the output; output X = NOT (AB).
A = 0, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 0, B = 1 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 0 -> X = 1
A = 1, B = 1 -> X = 0
Draw these five symbols with their truth tables on the chart and display it in the classroom.

Q: GROUP D 'CRT': CRT technology is replaced with LED and LCD technology for television screens. Identify the main reason behind this shift. Also discuss where the research is still progressing in CRT technology. Document your finding in an article for your school magazine.

Ans: Write the article in these steps. First, describe the CRT: it uses an electron gun and a long evacuated glass tube, so the set is bulky, deep and heavy, it consumes more electric power, and its picture size is limited. Then give the main reason for the shift: LED and LCD screens are flat, thin and light, consume much less power, can be made in large sizes with a sharper and brighter picture, and are cheaper to manufacture, so they have replaced the CRT in televisions and monitors. Finally, discuss where CRT research is still progressing: CRTs are still studied and improved for specialised uses where their fast response, high brightness and ability to work in harsh conditions are needed, such as some medical, industrial and scientific display equipment. End the article with a short conclusion and submit it to the school magazine.

Q: GROUP E 'TECHNOLOGY AND ELECTRONICS': Write an essay for your school magazine that modern world is the world of digital electronics. Identify by quoting examples that electronics is shifting from low-tech electrical appliances to high-tech electronic appliances. And that computers are the forefront of electronic technology.

Ans: Write the essay with this plan. Introduction: the modern world runs on digital electronics, in which signals are ON (1) or OFF (0) instead of continuously varying. Body, part 1 - the shift from low-tech electrical appliances to high-tech electronic appliances, with examples: the old electric fan and heater have gained electronic speed controllers and thermostats; the simple radio and television have become digital receivers and flat-screen TV; the telephone has become the mobile phone; music has shifted from tape recorders to CD players and digital players. Body, part 2 - computers at the forefront: computers control banking, education, hospitals, communication through the internet, and even other electronic machines, because they process digital information at very high speed. Conclusion: life today, from home appliances to communication, is governed by digital electronics, and computers lead this technology.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The components of an information and communication system are humans, hardware, software, procedures and data/information.
  • A signal is the electric or electromagnetic representation of data or information.
  • Signals are transmitted through optical fibres by total internal reflection.
  • An antenna is a conductor system used to radiate or collect electromagnetic energy.
  • The operating system is the software that allows users to interact with the computer system.
  • A flash drive stores and retrieves information with no moving parts.
  • The floppy is the information storage device least used these days.
  • Telephone communication transmits signals through electric wires.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: 1. The components of information and communication systems are humans, hardware, software, procedures and _____

Options: (a) computers (b) fields (c) data/informattion (d) signals

Correct answer: data/informattion

Q: 2. Electric or electromagnetic representations of data or information is termed as

Options: (a) computer (b) signal (c) transmission (d) software

Correct answer: signal

Q: 3. The phenomenon of total internal reflection is used in transmission of signal through

Options: (a) electric wires (b) optical fibers (c) electromagnetic waves (d) radio

Correct answer: optical fibers

Q: 4. Electrical conductor or system of conductors used either for radiating electromagnetic energy or for collecting electromagnetic energy is

Options: (a) antenna (b) satellite (c) repeater (d) signal

Correct answer: antenna

Q: 5. Software that allows users to interact with the computer system is

Options: (a) hardware (b) application (c) operating system (d) program

Correct answer: operating system

Q: 6. Which of the following information storage device has no moving parts to store and retrieve information

Options: (a) CD/DVD (b) Hard Drive (c) Flash drive (d) Floppy

Correct answer: Flash drive

Q: 7. Which of the following information storage device is least used these days

Options: (a) CD/DVD (b) Hard Drive (c) Flash drive (d) Floppy

Correct answer: Floppy

Q: 8. Telephone communication is the example of transmission of signals through

Options: (a) electric wires (b) optical fibres (c) electromagnetic waves (d) All

Correct answer: electric wires

mcqs.q: The components of information and communication systems are humans, hardware, software, procedures and _____
mcqs.why: The five components of an information and communication system are humans, hardware, software, procedures and data/information, the raw facts on which the whole system works.

mcqs.q: Electric or electromagnetic representations of data or information is termed as
mcqs.why: Data or information carried in electric or electromagnetic form is called a signal; it is the signal that actually travels through wires, optical fibres or air from sender to receiver.

mcqs.q: The phenomenon of total internal reflection is used in transmission of signal through
mcqs.why: Inside an optical fibre the light signal strikes the inner surface at a large angle and is reflected again and again by total internal reflection, so it travels along the fibre without escaping.

mcqs.q: Electrical conductor or system of conductors used either for radiating electromagnetic energy or for collecting electromagnetic energy is
mcqs.why: An antenna is the conductor system at each end of a radio link: the transmitting antenna radiates electromagnetic energy into space and the receiving antenna collects electromagnetic energy from space.

mcqs.q: Software that allows users to interact with the computer system is
mcqs.why: The operating system is the system software that manages the hardware and lets the user interact with the computer system, running applications and handling files, input and output.

mcqs.q: Which of the following information storage device has no moving parts to store and retrieve information
mcqs.why: A flash drive stores data electronically in flash memory with no moving parts, while a CD/DVD drive spins a disc, a hard drive spins platters and a floppy drive spins the disk.

mcqs.q: Which of the following information storage device is least used these days
mcqs.why: The floppy disk stores only 1.44 MB in its 3.5 inch form and has been replaced by hard drives, optical discs and flash drives, so it is the least used storage device these days.

mcqs.q: Telephone communication is the example of transmission of signals through
mcqs.why: In telephone communication the sound is converted into electrical signals in the mouthpiece, carried through electric wires, and converted back into sound in the earpiece at the other end.

mcqs.q: What is the storage capacity of a 3.5 inch floppy diskette?
mcqs.why: The book states that the 3.5 inch floppy diskette stores only 1.44 MB, which is far less than a CD at 700 MB or a DVD at 4.7 GB, and this small capacity is why floppies fell out of use.

mcqs.q: How much data can a DVD store?
mcqs.why: A DVD stores up to 4.7 GB of data in digital form, which the book notes is more than six times the typical 700 MB capacity of a compact disc (CD).

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Secondary storage is the reliable means of storing information because it stores data permanently and in large quantity even when the computer is switched off.
  • Data is a collection of raw facts and figures, while information is data processed and organised so that it becomes meaningful and useful.
  • Uplink and downlink use different frequency bands so the strong transmitted signal does not interfere with the weak received signal.
  • The cell in cell phone is the small geographical area around a tower within which the phone signal can be received.
  • The internet can be used for shopping, online banking, paying utility bills, investing and finding jobs.
  • A flash drive has no moving parts, connects through a built-in USB Type-A plug and needs no separate drive.
  • The hard disk drive is the most commonly used reliable store because of its very large capacity and permanent magnetic storage.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Conceptual Questions (Give a brief response to the following questions)

Q: 1. Identify the most reliable means of storing information?

Ans: Secondary storage devices are the reliable means of storing information because they store data permanently, in large quantity, even when the computer is switched off. Among them the hard disk drive is the most commonly used reliable store because of its very large capacity and permanent magnetic storage, and the flash drive is also highly reliable because it has no moving parts that can wear out or be damaged, unlike the optical drive and the hard drive.

Q: 2. How information is different from data?

Ans: Data is a collection of raw facts and figures; it is bits of information, but not information itself. When data is processed, interpreted, organised, structured or presented so that it becomes meaningful and useful, it is called information. For example, marks of students are data, while the prepared result showing positions and grades is information.

Q: 3. Why frequency band for uplink and downlink is different in transmission of microwaves through space?

Ans: In satellite communication the satellite receives the weak signal from the Earth station on one frequency band (uplink), amplifies it and sends it back to Earth on a different frequency band (downlink). The two bands are kept different so that the strong transmitted signal of the satellite does not interfere with, or drown, the weak signal it is receiving at the same time.

Q: 4. What does 'cell' in 'cell phone' refers to?

Ans: The 'cell' in cell phone refers to the small geographical area around a tower (antenna station) within which the phone's signal can be received. Each tower covers its own cell, typically an area of several miles, and as the user moves from one cell to another the call is handed over to the next tower.

Q: 5. Can internet be used for shopping? Give an example.

Ans: Yes, the internet is widely used for shopping as part of managing our daily life. For example, a person can visit an online store, select clothes, books or electronic items, pay for them through online banking or card, and the goods are delivered to the home. The internet is likewise used for paying utility bills, online banking, investing and finding jobs.

Q: 6. How a flash drive is different from other storage devices?

Ans: A flash drive is a small, ultra-portable secondary storage device. Unlike the hard drive and the optical (CD/DVD) drive, it has no moving parts to store and retrieve information, so it is faster, safer and less easily damaged. It connects to the computer through its built-in USB Type-A plug and does not need a separate drive to work.

mcqs.q: Why is secondary storage called a reliable means of storing information?
options: It is the fastest memory inside the computer
It stores data permanently in large quantity even when the computer is switched off
It stores data only while the computer is on
It can store only a very small amount of data
mcqs.why: Secondary storage keeps data permanently and in large quantity even with the power off, unlike primary memory which loses its contents, so it is the reliable long-term store of information.

mcqs.q: Which device is described as the most commonly used reliable store because of its very large capacity and permanent magnetic storage?
mcqs.why: The hard disk drive stores information permanently on magnetic platters with a very large capacity inside the computer, which makes it the most commonly used reliable store.

mcqs.q: What is data?
options: A collection of raw facts and figures
A prepared result showing positions and grades
A set of instructions for the computer
mcqs.why: Data is a collection of raw facts and figures; it is bits of information but not information itself, because it has not yet been processed into a meaningful and useful form.

mcqs.q: The marks of students by themselves are data. What is the prepared result showing positions and grades?
mcqs.why: When data is processed, interpreted, organised and presented so that it becomes meaningful and useful it is called information, so the prepared result with positions and grades is information, not raw data.

mcqs.q: Why are the uplink and downlink frequency bands different in satellite communication?
options: To make the signal travel faster
So the strong transmitted signal does not interfere with the weak signal being received
To reduce the cost of the satellite
So only one station can use the satellite
mcqs.why: The satellite receives a weak uplink signal and sends back a strong amplified downlink signal at the same time; different bands stop the strong transmitted signal from drowning the weak received signal.

mcqs.q: What does the word cell refer to in cell phone?
options: The SIM card inside the phone
The small geographical area around a tower within which the signal can be received
mcqs.why: Each tower or antenna station covers its own small geographical area called a cell, typically an area of several miles, and the phone works only while its signal can be received inside a cell.

mcqs.q: What happens when a cell phone user moves from one cell to another?
options: The call is handed over to the next tower
A new number is allotted to the phone
mcqs.why: The network of towers is arranged in cells, and as the user crosses from one cell into the next the call is handed over to the next tower so the conversation continues without a break.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of using the internet for shopping?
options: Watching a film on a DVD player
Paying a shopkeeper in cash at a market
Selecting goods in an online store, paying online and getting them delivered home
mcqs.why: Internet shopping means visiting an online store, selecting items such as clothes, books or electronic goods, paying through online banking or card, and having the goods delivered to the home.

mcqs.q: How does a flash drive connect to a computer?
options: Through its built-in USB Type-A plug
mcqs.why: A flash drive is a small ultra-portable device with its own built-in USB Type-A plug, so it connects directly to the computer and does not need a separate drive to work.

mcqs.q: Why is a flash drive less easily damaged than a hard drive or an optical drive?
options: It has no moving parts to wear out or be damaged
It stores data on magnetic tape
mcqs.why: The hard drive and the optical drive have moving parts that can wear out or be damaged, while the flash drive has no moving parts at all, which makes it faster, safer and less easily damaged.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • ICT is the technology used to create, access, analyse, store, transmit and communicate information electronically.
  • The components of ICT are data and information, hardware, software, procedures and human resource.
  • In the flow of information the source produces information, the transmitter converts it into a signal, the transmission system carries it and the receiver converts it back.
  • Light signals travel inside an optical fibre by total internal reflection after an LED or injection laser diode converts electrical signals into light.
  • A fax machine scans a document one line at a time and needs about one minute for one page.
  • Primary storage is temporary, internal and the fastest, while secondary storage stores information permanently and in large quantity.
  • A CD typically stores 700 MB and a DVD stores up to 4.7 GB, more than six times a CD.
  • Data management is acquiring, validating, storing, protecting and processing data so it stays accessible, reliable and timely.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Comprehensive Questions (Give an extended response to the following questions)

Q: 1. What is Information and Communication Technology (ICT)? Explain briefly its components.

Ans: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is the infrastructure and components that enable modern computing; it is the technology used to create, access, analyse, store, transmit and communicate information electronically. Its components are: (A) Data and information - the raw facts and the processed, meaningful form of data on which the system works. (B) Hardware - the physical parts of the system that can be touched, such as the mouse, keyboard and printer. (C) Software - the applications and programming instructions that tell the hardware what to do. (D) Procedures - the instructions, rules and guidelines given in manuals for using the system correctly. (E) Human resource (people) - the people who design and operate the software, feed input data and build the hardware.

Q: 2. Explain the flow of information. Describe how information is transmitted as electric signal through wires, light signals through optical fibres and radio waves through air/vacuum?

Ans: The flow of information is the path or means followed by information entities from the sender to the receiver; in a communication system the source produces the information, the transmitter converts it into a signal, the transmission system carries it, and the receiver converts it back for the destination.
Through wires: the information is converted into electrical signals at the transmitter and sent through metal wires such as twisted pair or coaxial cable. In telephone communication, sound is converted into electrical signals in the mouthpiece, carried by wires, and converted back into sound in the earpiece at the other end. Analogue signals are boosted by amplifiers after every few kilometres, and digital signals are regenerated by repeaters after about every kilometre.
Through optical fibres: the information is first converted into electrical voltage signals and then into light signals by an LED or injection laser diode (ILD). The light travels inside the glass fibre by total internal reflection and is converted back at the receiving end. Step-index multimode fibres are used for short distances, single-mode fibres for long distances such as telephone and cable TV networks, and graded-index multimode fibres for local area networks.
Through air/vacuum as radio waves: the transmitting antenna converts radio-frequency electrical energy into electromagnetic energy and radiates it into the atmosphere, space or water. The receiving antenna collects the electromagnetic energy and converts it back into electrical signals. Radio broadcasting and satellite communication (uplink and downlink) work in this way.

Q: 3. Describe function and use of fax machine, cell phone, photo phone and computer.

Ans: Fax machine: it sends a copy of a document over the telephone line. The sending part works like a scanner; it scans the document one line at a time in black and white, using one type of pulse for black and another for white. The line transmits the pulses almost instantly, and the receiving machine controls a printer to reproduce the document; about one minute is needed for one page.
Cell phone: it is a wireless telephone that sends and receives signals through towers. Besides calls, it is used to store contacts and to-do lists, send and receive text messages, set appointments and reminders, use a calculator, get information from the internet, send and receive email, and run downloadable applications through its operating system.
Photo phone (photophone): it transmits speech (sound) on a beam of light instead of wires. Such optical communication became practical with the development of the laser and laser diode in the 1960s and of low-loss optical fibres in the 1970s.
Computer: it is a device that can be instructed to carry out sequences of arithmetic and logical operations automatically through programming. Its types include the mainframe computer, desktop/personal computer, laptop/notebook, tablet and smartphone, used in offices, education, business, banks and homes for processing and storing information.

Q: 4. What is email and internet? List few uses of internet in daily life.

Ans: The internet is a worldwide system of computer networks - a network of networks - that links computers all over the world so that information can be shared. Email (electronic mail) is a method of exchanging messages between people using electronic devices; it operates across computer networks, primarily the internet, and has practically replaced the postal service for short written transactions.
Uses of the internet in daily life: communication through email, social media, blogs, chat rooms, forums and VOIP calls; exploring the world and keeping up with events and news; managing life through online banking, online shopping, paying utility bills, investing, calendars and finding jobs; study and research; and entertainment such as music, videos and games.

Q: 5. What are information storage devices? Describe the use of information storage devices such as audio cassettes, video cassettes, hard discs, floppy, compact discs and flash drive.

Ans: Information storage devices are devices used to store data and information. Primary storage is temporary, internal and the fastest (such as RAM and cache), while secondary storage stores information permanently and in large quantity, e.g. hard disk, optical disk drive and USB flash drive.
Audio cassettes: magnetic tape on which music and sounds are recorded; data is read and written in sequence, so they are used mainly for storing (archival) purposes and need a special player.
Video cassettes: magnetic tape that stores video along with sound, played through a video player; like audio cassettes they are sequential-access storage.
Hard disk (HDD): it consists of one or more platters with a magnetic head in an air-sealed casing; it permanently stores and retrieves large amounts of information inside the computer.
Floppy disk: a thin flexible magnetic disk in a square plastic carrier, used in a floppy disk drive (FDD); the 3.5 inch diskette stores only 1.44 MB, and floppies were used for distributing software, transferring files, backups and storing the operating system.
Compact disc (CD): a portable device that records, stores and plays back audio, video and other data in digital form, with a typical capacity of 700 MB; a DVD stores up to 4.7 GB, more than six times a CD.
Flash drive: a small, ultra-portable storage device with no moving parts, connected through a built-in USB Type-A plug, used to carry and transfer information between computers.

Q: 6. What are the functions of word processing?

Ans: Word processing is used for creating documents on a computer. Its functions are: creating, editing, saving and printing documents; copying, pasting, moving and deleting text within a document; formatting text, such as changing font type, bolding, underlining and italicizing; creating and editing tables; inserting elements from other software, such as illustrations and photographs; correcting spelling and grammar; and performing repetitive tasks such as mail merge, in which personalised letters are produced from a database.

Q: 7. How information is handled? Describe data management and its monitoring and control.

Ans: Handling information means using ICT for gathering, organising, storing, retrieving, modifying, interpreting and presenting information, for which databases, spreadsheets and the internet are used.
Data management is the administrative process of acquiring, validating, storing, protecting and processing data so that it remains accessible, reliable and timely for its users. It involves three main activities: assessing the needs of the organisation and selecting a suitable data platform; developing standard operating procedures (SOPs) and training the staff; and making the data available in a suitable format for decision making.
Monitoring and control is the process of overseeing all the tasks and metrics needed to ensure that a project stays within its scope, finishes on time and within budget, and carries minimum risk. It compares the actual performance with the planned performance and takes corrective action where needed, and it continues throughout the life of the project.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the components of ICT?
options: Data and information, hardware, software, procedures and human resource
mcqs.why: ICT has five components: data and information, hardware that can be touched, software that tells the hardware what to do, procedures given in manuals, and the human resource who design, operate and use the system.

mcqs.q: In the flow of information, what does the transmitter do?
options: It converts the information into a signal
It prints the information on paper
It buys the information from the source
mcqs.why: The source produces the information and the transmitter converts it into a signal; the transmission system then carries the signal and the receiver converts it back for the destination.

mcqs.q: How are analogue and digital signals maintained over long distances in wires?
options: Analogue signals are regenerated by repeaters and digital signals are boosted by amplifiers after every few kilometres
Analogue signals are boosted by amplifiers and digital signals are also boosted by amplifiers after every few kilometres
Analogue signals are regenerated by repeaters after about every kilometre and digital signals are boosted by amplifiers
Analogue signals are boosted by amplifiers after every few kilometres and digital signals are regenerated by repeaters after about every kilometre
mcqs.why: Analogue signals weaken along the wire and are boosted by amplifiers after every few kilometres, while digital signals are cleaned up and regenerated by repeaters after about every kilometre.

mcqs.q: Which fibre type is used for long distances such as telephone and cable TV networks?
mcqs.why: The book assigns step-index multimode fibres to short distances, graded-index multimode fibres to local area networks, and single-mode fibres to long distances such as telephone and cable TV networks.

mcqs.q: How does the sending part of a fax machine read a document?
options: It photographs the whole page at once
It reads only the headings of the page
It scans the document one line at a time in black and white, using one type of pulse for black and another for white
It types the document again on a keyboard
mcqs.why: The sending part of a fax machine works like a scanner, reading the document one line at a time in black and white with different pulses for black and white; the receiving machine then prints the copy, taking about one minute per page.

mcqs.q: What is a photophone (photo phone)?
options: A device that transmits speech on a beam of light instead of wires
A telephone with a large display screen
mcqs.why: The photophone transmits speech (sound) on a beam of light instead of wires; such optical communication became practical with the laser and laser diode in the 1960s and low-loss optical fibres in the 1970s.

mcqs.q: Which statement about primary and secondary storage is correct?
options: Primary storage is permanent and secondary storage is temporary
Primary storage is temporary, internal and the fastest, while secondary storage is permanent and large
Primary and secondary storage are permanent
Secondary storage is the fastest memory
mcqs.why: Primary storage such as RAM and cache is temporary, internal and the fastest, while secondary storage such as the hard disk, optical disk and USB flash drive stores information permanently and in large quantity.

mcqs.q: Audio and video cassettes store data on magnetic tape. How is the data accessed?
options: Randomly from any point at once
In sequence, so they are used mainly for storing (archival) purposes
mcqs.why: On audio and video cassettes the data is recorded on magnetic tape and is read and written in sequence, so a special player must wind through the tape and the cassettes are used mainly for archival storage.

mcqs.q: Which function of word processing produces personalised letters from a database?
mcqs.why: Mail merge is the word processing function for repetitive tasks in which personalised letters are produced from a database, alongside other functions such as creating, editing, formatting text and correcting spelling and grammar.

mcqs.q: What does monitoring and control of a project compare?
options: The actual performance with the planned performance, taking corrective action where needed
mcqs.why: Monitoring and control oversees a project so it stays within scope, on time and within budget with minimum risk; it compares actual performance with planned performance and takes corrective action where needed.

lessons.title: Projects
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • ICT benefits society through fast and cheap worldwide transfer of information and better education, banking, shopping, health and government services.
  • Risks of ICT include loss of personal privacy, hacking and fraud, health problems such as eye strain and screen addiction, and electronic waste harming the environment.
  • High-tech communication such as email and cell phone messages reaches in seconds over worldwide distances, while a traditional letter by post takes days.
  • Computer technology is used in education, health, banking, business, communication, transport, entertainment, home and government work.
  • Virtual reality is an artificial environment created with software that the user accepts as real, used in tourism for virtual tours of places and museums.

Solved Exercises

Projects

Q: GROUP A 'RISKS AND BENEFITS OF ICT': Assess the risks and benefits to society and the environment of introducing ICT (e.g. effects on personal privacy, criminal activities, health and transfer of information). Write an essay to be published in school magazine.

Ans: Write the essay in this order. Benefits: ICT makes the transfer of information fast and cheap across the whole world; it helps education, banking, shopping, health services and government work; people can communicate instantly by email, chat and video calls. Risks to society: loss of personal privacy because personal data stored on networks can be stolen or misused; criminal activities such as hacking, fraud and spreading false information become easier; health problems such as eye strain, poor posture and addiction to screens increase; and people who have no access to ICT are left behind. Effects on the environment: ICT saves paper and travel, but discarded computers and phones (electronic waste) and the electricity used by large networks harm the environment. Conclude that ICT is beneficial when it is used carefully with proper laws for privacy and safety, and submit the essay to the school magazine.

Q: GROUP B 'ADVANTAGES OF HIGH TECH COMMUNICATION DEVICES': Compare the advantages of high-tech communication devices with the traditional system through library or internet search. Prepare a chart and give a brief presentation to your class fellows.

Ans: Search the library or the internet and compare the two systems point by point on the chart. Speed: a letter by post takes days, while email, fax and cell phone messages reach in seconds. Distance: traditional communication is slow over long distances, while modern devices communicate worldwide instantly through wires, optical fibres and satellites. Cost: modern communication is much cheaper per message. Storage: information in modern devices is stored electronically in small devices with huge capacity, while traditional records need large paper files. Facilities: modern devices also give pictures, video, internet, banking and entertainment along with talking, which the traditional system cannot. Draw the comparison as a two-column chart and present it to the class.

Q: GROUP C 'CHART MAKING': Prepare a chart listing the use of computer technology in various fields of daily life, to be displayed in your class room.

Ans: Make the chart with the field in one column and the use of computer technology in the other. Education: online learning, digital libraries and results. Health: patient records, diagnosis and hospital management. Banking: ATM machines, online banking and transfer of money. Business: accounts, stock records, online shopping and advertising. Communication: email, social media, chat and video calling. Transport: booking of tickets, traffic control and navigation. Entertainment: games, music and films. Home: paying utility bills, calendars and finding jobs and information. Government and offices: records, word processing and data management. Display the completed chart in the classroom.

Q: GROUP D 'MAKING NEWSLETTER': Newsletters are usually produced for a specific audience, having words and images. Find a computer and by using a word processing software (Like Microsoft word) make a news letter including last year events of your school, make a hard copy (printed document) available for school library.

Ans: Follow these steps. (1) Collect the material: last year's school events such as examinations and results, sports day, science exhibition, prize distribution, trips and important visits. (2) Open a word processing software such as Microsoft Word and create a new document; use its functions of creating, editing, saving and formatting text, choose suitable fonts, bold headings and insert tables where needed. (3) Insert photographs and illustrations of the events from other software, and correct spelling and grammar with the built-in tools. (4) Arrange the newsletter in sections with a title, school name and date, written for its specific audience of students and teachers. (5) Save the file, print a hard copy and place the printed newsletter in the school library.

Q: GROUP E 'VIRTUAL REALITY (VR)': Research the current state of VR technology, including virtual immersion and think about how this technology could be used, for example, in tourism. Write a research article for the school magazine.

Ans: Write the research article with these contents. Definition from research: virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment created with software and presented to the user in such a way that the user believes and accepts it as a real environment; the user wears a headset like thick goggles and experiences virtual immersion, feeling present inside the artificial world. Present state: VR is already used for testing product designs before manufacture, in flight simulators for training pilots, and in medical training where doctors practise safely. Use in tourism: a person can take a virtual tour of historical places, museums and cities from home, which helps tourists choose and plan real trips, and lets people who cannot travel still visit famous places. Conclude with the future growth of VR and submit the article to the school magazine.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The number of neutrons in a nucleus is N = A - Z, so plutonium 242/92 Pu has 242 - 92 = 150 neutrons.
  • Alpha and beta decay each produce a new element because they change the atomic number, while gamma decay does not.
  • Gamma decay leaves the numbers of protons and neutrons unchanged.
  • Alpha decay produces the greatest mass and charge loss of the three decay types.
  • Radium-226 emits an alpha particle and forms radon as the daughter nucleus.
  • A sample reduces to half in exactly one half-life, so argon-39 with a half-life of 269 yr halves in 269 years.
  • The energy of the sun and stars comes from nuclear fusion.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: 1. What is the number of neutrons in the plutonium 242/92 Pu

Options: (a) 92 (b) 142 (c) 150 (d) 242

Correct answer: 150

Q: 2. Which one or more of the three decay processes (α, β, or γ) results in a new element?

Options: (a) Only α (b) Only β (c) Only γ (d) α and β

Correct answer: α and β

Q: 3. What type of nuclear decay leaves the number of protons and neutrons unchanged?

Options: (a) alpha decay (b) beta decay (c) gamma decay (d) both A & B

Correct answer: gamma decay

Q: 4. What type of nuclear decay most often produces the greatest mass and charge loss?

Options: (a) alpha decay (b) beta decay (c) gamma decay (d) both B & C

Correct answer: alpha decay

Q: 5. 214/84 Po undergoes α-decay to produce a daughter nucleus that itself undergoes B- decay. Which one of the following nuclei is the one that ultimately results? (A) 211/82 Pb (B) 215/80 Hg (C) 211/81 Tl (D) 212/83 Bi

Ans: Step 1 (alpha decay): 214/84 Po -> 210/82 Pb + 4/2 He (mass number 214 - 4 = 210, atomic number 84 - 2 = 82).
Step 2 (beta-minus decay of the daughter): 210/82 Pb -> 210/83 Bi + beta particle (mass number stays 210, atomic number 82 + 1 = 83).
Answer: the nucleus that ultimately results is 210/83 Bi.
Note: no printed option is exactly correct. Option (D) 212/83 Bi names the right element (bismuth, Z = 83) but its mass number should be 210, not 212 - a misprint in the book's option list.

Q: 6. Radium-226 decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the daughter nucleus?

Options: (a) Rd (b) Rn (c) Bi (d) Pb

Correct answer: Rn

Q: 7. 39Ar is an isotope with a half-life of 269 yr. It will reduce to half in

Options: (a) 134.5 min (b) 134.5 Years (c) 269 min (d) 269 Years

Correct answer: 269 Years

Q: 8. A sample starts with 1000 radioactive atoms. How many halflives have elapsed when 750 atoms have decayed?

Options: (a) 0.25 (b) 1.5 (c) 2.0 (d) 2.5

Correct answer: 2.0

Q: 9. Origin of energy from the sun and stars is

Options: (a) fission (b) fusion (c) Carbon dating (d) radioactivity

Correct answer: fusion

mcqs.q: What is the number of neutrons in the plutonium 242/92 Pu
mcqs.why: Number of neutrons N = A - Z = 242 - 92 = 150. The value 92 is the number of protons and 242 is the total number of nucleons, so the neutron count is 150.

mcqs.q: Which one or more of the three decay processes (α, β, or γ) results in a new element?
mcqs.why: A new element forms when the atomic number Z changes: alpha decay lowers Z by 2 and beta decay raises Z by 1, while gamma decay changes only the energy and leaves the element the same.

mcqs.q: What type of nuclear decay leaves the number of protons and neutrons unchanged?
mcqs.why: In gamma decay the nucleus only loses excess energy as gamma rays, written A/Z X* -> A/Z X + γ, so the numbers of protons and neutrons, and therefore A and Z, stay unchanged.

mcqs.q: What type of nuclear decay most often produces the greatest mass and charge loss?
mcqs.why: An alpha particle carries away 4 units of mass number and 2 units of charge, while a beta particle changes no mass number and only 1 unit of charge, and gamma rays carry away neither mass nor charge.

mcqs.q: 214/84 Po undergoes α-decay to produce a daughter nucleus that itself undergoes B- decay. Which one of the following nuclei is the one that ultimately results?
mcqs.why: Step 1, alpha decay: A = 214 - 4 = 210 and Z = 84 - 2 = 82, giving 210/82 Pb. Step 2, beta-minus decay: A stays 210 and Z = 82 + 1 = 83, giving 210/83 Bi. The book prints this option as 212/83 Bi, which is a misprint; the correct mass number is 210.

mcqs.q: Radium-226 decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the daughter nucleus?
mcqs.why: Alpha decay lowers the atomic number by 2, from Z = 88 for radium to Z = 86, and the element with atomic number 86 is radon, symbol Rn.

mcqs.q: 39Ar is an isotope with a half-life of 269 yr. It will reduce to half in
mcqs.why: By definition the half life is the time taken for half of the sample to decay, so argon-39 with a half life of 269 yr reduces to half in exactly 269 years, not in half of that time.

mcqs.q: A sample starts with 1000 radioactive atoms. How many halflives have elapsed when 750 atoms have decayed?
mcqs.why: Atoms remaining = 1000 - 750 = 250. Fraction remaining = (1/2)^n = 250/1000 = 1/4 = (1/2)^2, so n = 2 half lives have elapsed: 1000 -> 500 -> 250.

mcqs.q: Origin of energy from the sun and stars is
mcqs.why: In the sun and stars light nuclei join together in nuclear fusion, the proton-proton cycle, and the mass lost appears as energy; fission is the splitting of heavy nuclei and is not the source of stellar energy.

mcqs.q: How many neutrons are contained in a gold nucleus 197/79 Au?
mcqs.why: Number of neutrons N = A - Z. Substituting A = 197 and Z = 79 gives N = 197 - 79 = 118, so the gold nucleus contains 118 neutrons and 79 protons.

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Ordinary hydrogen 1/1 H is the only nuclide whose atomic number equals its mass number, with one proton and no neutron.
